sections.title: Autonomy Is Already on the Water.
sections.lede: Ten thousand hours of flight control. Perception now collecting on every hull. Vehicle autonomy on the N30 this month.

rungs.label: Flight control
rungs.body: NavierOS flies the foils hundreds of times a second — 10,000+ operating hours on the N30. Every autonomy layer sits on this core.

rungs.label: Perception
rungs.body: Vision-first, sensor-fused. Cameras on every hull; stereo depth, live scene segmentation and 3D harbor mapping from real Bay Area and Idaho operations. 74,000+ images captured in a single week of demos. Radar and AIS fusion being added.

rungs.label: Vehicle autonomy
rungs.body: Heading hold, waypoint following and station-keeping running in simulation, commanded from the helm and a ground control station. On-water N30 trials — Q4 2026, first milestone filmed by December.

rungs.label: Detect and avoid
rungs.body: Advisory detect-and-avoid rides beside the operator on every sea trial — every trial adds to the autonomy record. Assisted docking follows.

sections.fleet_data_line: Every vessel logs perception, telemetry and energy data to a central fleet database — the dataset compounds with every hull delivered.

media.caption: What the boat sees — raw camera feeds (left) and live scene segmentation: sky, land, water, vessel, people (right). N30 operations, Idaho, August 2026.
Stereo depth on a dock approach — left camera, point cloud, depth map. Pilings, dock edge and hulls resolved in 3D from a bow-mounted stereo camera. Sausalito, August 2026.
The boat maps its own harbor — shoreline and docks reconstructed in 3D from the run itself, track overlaid. Alameda estuary, August 2026.
Waypoint following and heading hold in simulation, commanded from the NavierOS helm display — the same screen the operator uses on the water.
